key_insight: A parametric PINN and a tensorial reduced-order model can both learn a direct map for shallow-water dam-break solutions without time integration, but shock-aware collocation is critical for PINN robustness.
engineering_relevance: These surrogate models can accelerate uncertainty studies and parametric sweeps for hydraulic transients by replacing costly full-order shallow-water simulations.
method: Parametric PINN learns solution state from space, time, and dam-break parameters.
Non-intrusive TROM builds a reduced model from tensorial structure of the solution map.
Shock-aware collocation is added to better handle discontinuities in the PINN.
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates both models on out-of-sample and extrapolated parameter values for the 1D shallow-water dam-break problem.
watch_item: Accuracy and robustness near shocks are sensitive; without shock-aware sampling, the PINN may struggle on discontinuous flow features.
paper_title: Comparison of a Parametric Physics-Informed Neural Network and a Tensorial Reduced-Order Model for the Shallow-Water Dam-Break Problem
